4.4 Zona comune e suoi limiti (Limite A,: 4.4 Common zone and its limits (Limit A, Limit B)
L'articolo [1] individua gli incroci del: The article [1] identifies the intersections of the curves where the horizon of each station meets the E layer. They are the intersections of two circles of angular radius ρ = dH/r centred on A and B:
Se 1 − |p0|² < 0 la tratta è più lunga d: If 1 − |p0|² < 0 the path is longer than 2·dH and the two stations do not see a common zone of the E layer.
Questi due punti sono i bordi più lontan: These two points are the farthest edges of the E-layer zone seen by both stations, not the points where most reflections arrive. On the path JN70CN–IN78UO (1710 km, azimuth 308°) they lie 1062 km from the station, 37° to the left and right of the direct direction: too far to the side for pointing. The program calls them "Limit A" and "Limit B" and draws them faintly on the map, together with the two circles of the common zone.
4.5 Hot A e Hot B (hot spot per il punta: 4.5 Hot A and Hot B (hot spots for pointing)
Le riflessioni delle meteore sporadiche: Reflections from sporadic meteors concentrate in two zones ("hot spots") on either side of the path midpoint. J. Richardson (AMS) [23], in the table quoted by DJ5HG [22], gives the antenna offset from the direct direction: 13° at 1000 km, 11° at 1250 km, 10° at 1500 and at 2000 km. AMS Bulletin No. 203, quoted by W8WN [15], gives 10° at 1500 and 1800 km.
Hot A e Hot B sono i punti a distanza s: Hot A and Hot B are the points at distance s from the midpoint, perpendicular to the path (A on the left looking from the station towards the DX station, B on the right). With the "auto (AMS)" checkbox ticked (the default) s comes from the offset in Richardson's table, linearly interpolated (13° below 1000 km, 10° above 2000 km): s = (D/2)·tan(offset). Unticking the checkbox lets you enter s by hand (MSHV [16] uses 150 km).
Lo scarto dalla direzione diretta, visto: The offset from the direct direction, seen from the station, is to a good approximation:
Con la tabella AMS: 1000 km → 13°, s ≈ 1: With the AMS table: 1000 km → 13°, s ≈ 115 km; 1250 km → 11°, s ≈ 121 km; 1500 km → 10°, s ≈ 132 km; 2000 km → 10°, s ≈ 176 km. JN70CN-IN78UO (1710 km) → 10°, s ≈ 151 km, like the 150 km used previously and by MSHV; on short paths the table brings the hot spots closer to the midpoint.
4.6 Hot consigliato dall'efficienza: 4.6 Hot spot recommended by the efficiency
Per l'ora mostrata sulla volta celeste i: For the time shown on the Sky view the program sums, over all showers above the horizon, the weight ZHR·η/100 split between side A (fraction fA, chapter 5.5) and side B. The hot spot on the side with the larger weight is the recommended one and appears in red on the map:
Lo spostamento di 10–30° verso il lato d: The shift of 10–30° towards the side of the reflections (side-scatter) is given in the article [1].
DJ5HG, riportato da DF5HC [17]: la rifle: DJ5HG, quoted by DF5HC [17]: reflection takes place on a cone around the trail; for shorter paths the antennas should be pointed to the side of the direct direction, both stations towards the same point, and depending on the radiant position one of the two points (HOT-A or HOT-B) is more favourable. It is the same criterion as the program's recommendation.
L'efficienza indica in percentuale quant: The efficiency indicates as a percentage how much the position of the shower allows reflections on a path (OH5IY [2], taken up in the article [1]); MCG_MS [3] calculates it for four fixed directions and, with the DX station's locator, for the real path.
Una scia rimanda il segnale tra A e B so: A trail sends the signal between A and B only if it is tangent to an ellipsoid with A and B at its foci (McKinley [8]). The trails of a shower are parallel to the radiant direction [1, 8]. For a point P of the E layer, with the unit vectors towards the stations:
La stessa legge è alla base di QTFGUI di: The same law underlies DJ5HG's QTFGUI: the ray that hits the trail is scattered on a cone around it, and only those on the cone receive the signal. The cone condition is equivalent to ŝ·n̂ = 0. [18, 22] In his 2004 text DJ5HG describes it like this: the trail crosses the E layer, the two antennas illuminate it and the receiver lies on the cone that has the trail as its axis; the wall of the cone is the lobe of a radiator thousands of wavelengths long, hence narrow, but at grazing incidence (long paths) it touches the ground over a wide area.
La condizione si accetta con una tollera: The condition is accepted with a Gaussian tolerance of σ = 0.05 rad (about 3°). For an ideal trail the wall of the cone is much narrower [22]; the 3° represent what the ideal cone does not see: the spread of the radiants of a shower (0.3-1.4° measured by the GMN), the trail bent by the wind and its finite length:
Per il meteor scatter QTFGUI di DJ5HG di: For meteor scatter DJ5HG's QTFGUI draws deviations from the reflection law of up to 32°: the program's Gaussian tolerance of 0.05 rad is stricter and concentrates the weight on almost exactly specular points. With 5 km sampling instead of 15 km the percentages change by less than 0.3 points. [18]
Potenza di una scia sottodensa (McKinley: Power of an underdense trail (McKinley [8]; ITU-R P.843 [28], eq. 3): proportional to λ³ / [R1 R2 (R1+R2) (1 − cos²β sin²φ)], with R1 = |A−P|, R2 = |B−P|, φ half the scattering angle and β the angle between the trail and the propagation plane A-P-B. With p̂ the unit normal to the plane, sin β = |ŝ·p̂|:
Fino alla versione 1.6 il programma pren: Up to version 1.6 the program took β = 0 for all trails, i.e. the weight 1/[R1 R2 (R1+R2) cos²φ]: trails crossing the plane of the path weighed up to 1/cos²φ times too much, 10-15 dB between 600 and 2000 km. From 1.7 β can be calculated for each point and each radiant direction with the option "Angle β between trail and path (full McKinley)", on by default because it gives the most cautious values (no trail is overestimated); turning the option off uses β = 0 as before. The correction was prompted by comparison with the page of GM8JBJ [9], which reports G4BAO's figure of about 6 dB less for trails aligned with the path.
φ limitato a 85° per evitare valori infi: φ limited to 85° to avoid infinite values in grazing directions.
Il numero di meteore che arrivano in un: The number of meteors arriving at a point is proportional to the sine of the radiant elevation at that point (the same correction used by the IMO for the ZHR [5]): ŝ·ûP.
Opzione \"Scie più lunghe con il radiant: Option "Longer trails with a low radiant (DJ5HG)", off by default, in Efficiency calculation: DJ5HG [22] observes that with a low radiant fewer meteors fall per km² but the trails are longer (up to 100 km usable) and satisfy the reflection law more often. With the option on the weight becomes min(sin El, 15/100): the usable thickness of the layer, 15 km, divided by the sine of the elevation gives the trail length, limited to 100 km. Above about 9° of elevation the two effects cancel out; with the option off, the calculation stays cautious.
Impostazioni pronte del calcolo, nella s: Calculation presets, on the same row: "Cautious" (the default, the most cautious values: height from the radar, normal trails, with β), "As DJ5HG" (102 km, long trails, with β) and "Custom", which is selected automatically when the height, the "from radar" checkbox, the long trails or the angle β are changed by hand.
Effetto dell'angolo β sulla direzione mi: Effect of the angle β on the best direction, 1000 km path: without β the maximum lies between 15° and 90° from the path depending on the radiant elevation (30° with the radiant at 30°, perpendicular with the radiant at 60°) and the perpendicular radiant is worth 67 % with the radiant at 30°; with β the maximum is always with the radiant along the path and the perpendicular radiant drops to 15 %. With β the best-direction rule of SM6FHZ and DH9GCD is therefore lost: β remains an option: it is on by default because it gives the most cautious values (no trail overestimated), and turning it off brings back the rule.
I punti P si campionano ogni 15 km alla: The points P are sampled every 15 km at height H, only where both stations see the point above the minimum elevation of the lobe. For each radiant direction:
F si calcola una volta per tratta su una: F is calculated once per path on a grid of directions (azimuth every 5°, elevation every 2.5°, in the midpoint frame) and then bilinearly interpolated.
Accanto alla percentuale, che vale per q: Next to the percentage, which applies to that path only, the program gives the efficiency in dB relative to the fixed reference of DJ5HG [22]: 0 dB is the maximum of a 1000 km north-south path straddling the equator with the radiant on the celestial equator at the equinox (the radiant rises in the east, passes through the zenith and sets in the west), calculated with the same height and the same weights. In this way different paths can be compared with each other. DJ5HG states an accuracy better than 6 dB for his values.
Una scia rimanda il segnale tra le due s: A trail sends the signal between the two stations only if it is tangent to an ellipsoid with the stations at its foci: at each point of the E layer only the radiants on the semicircle of the sky perpendicular to the bisector of the scattering angle are useful (Eshleman and Mlodnosky [24]; Meeks and James [25]). Near the midpoint this semicircle rises highest across the path: a radiant at elevation El produces specular trails about H·tan El to the side of the midpoint, on the side opposite the radiant, i.e. in the hot spots that Eshleman and Mlodnosky and Recommendation ITU-R P.843 [28] place about 100 km on either side. The number of trails and their ionisation increase with sin El [25]. The dependence of the echoes on the radiant position was calculated by Hines [26] and verified on four showers by Forsyth, Hines and Vogan [27]. From this follows the practical rule of SM6FHZ [4]: best path orthogonal to the radiant azimuth, pointing Az ± 90°, tolerance ±40-50°.
Riserva di DJ5HG [22]: con il radiante b: Reservation by DJ5HG [22]: with a low radiant lying right along the path McKinley's formula gives strong signals, even though the meteors are few (Hamburg-Narvik, Quadrantids, around 19 UTC). The rule "radiant aligned with the path = almost zero efficiency" therefore holds for a high radiant, not for a grazing one. The program stays cautious and does not raise the efficiency, but shows "LOW RADIANT ALONG THE PATH" on the Sky view when an active shower has its radiant below 20° and within 30° of the path direction. The gap with the radiant at the zenith between the two stations is confirmed (Quadrantids, Hamburg-Barcelona, around 08 UTC).
Termine di confronto indipendente: la fo: Independent term of comparison: the formula of DH9GCD quoted by DF5HC [17], with El and Az the elevation and azimuth of the radiant and P the azimuth of the DX station. It is maximum for El = 45° and P − Az = 90°; DF5HC considers the radiant too low below 20° and too high above 70°. It takes no account of distance or heights:
La formula di DH9GCD non ha una fonte pr: The DH9GCD formula has no published primary source: it combines the factor sin El (number and ionisation of the trails) with a factor cos El that represents how far the specular point moves away from the centre of the path as the radiant rises. Calculated with the radiant seen from the midpoint, as MS-Soft [29] does, it reproduces the MS-Soft table for KP30HV-JO52MM (1324 km, Quadrantids, 4/1/2001) within 4 points between 16° and 48° of elevation and within 16 points up to 64°, with the same maximum at 13 UT (96 % versus 92 %). It remains a term of comparison.
Nella sottolinguetta \"Calcolo prevision: In the sub-tab "Forecast calculation › Efficiency calculation" the program shows under each shower, in light blue, the formula as a percentage of its maximum, with El and Az seen from the station and P the azimuth of the DX station; with the symbol ↑ (and a warning on the Sky view) it flags a radiant above 70°:
Confronto con QTFGUI di DJ5HG (esempio d: Comparison with DJ5HG's QTFGUI (example from its manual): path Hamburg JO53IM - Barcelona, Quadrantids, 4 January. At 07:00 UTC QTFGUI gives pointing 252°, elevation 1°, relative effectiveness -8 dB, radiant in the reflection zone az. 83° el. 75°; at 08:00 no reflection zone; at 09:00 pointing 168°, elevation 2°, -4 dB, radiant az. 292° el. 74°. The program's model (height 102 km like QTFGUI) gives at 07:00 241°, 0°, -5.4 dB, radiant az. 77° el. 74°; at 08:00 0.6 % (-22 dB), i.e. practically zero; at 09:00 161°, 4°, -4.0 dB, radiant az. 286° el. 75°. DH9GCD gives 26 %, 2 % and 32 %: all three methods see the 08:00 gap, with the radiant almost at the zenith [18].
Confronto con le curve di DJ5HG [22] (Bi: Comparison with the curves of DJ5HG [22] (Bild 8 and 9: from Hamburg and from Munich, Quadrantids, 4 January), read from the plot (about ±0.5 dB and ±15 min) and compared with the program's automatic test (--prova-dj5hg, one value per hour). Times: the gap with the radiant near the zenith falls in the same hours (Barcelona 7.5–8.5 UTC in DJ5HG, 7–9 in the program; Sofia 6.6–7.8 and 7–8; Narvik 7–8.5 and 7–9); Moscow is closed from 3 to 10 in both, and the program confirms DJ5HG's text: from Hamburg open until about 2:30, from Munich until about 0:30. Pointing: deviations of 2–10° (Barcelona 225° and 233° versus 223° and 235° before the gap, 160° versus 169° after; Moscow 84° versus 82°, 79° versus 76°; Narvik jumps towards 338° at 20:40 in DJ5HG, between 20 and 21 in the program). Levels and shape, at 102 km (mean deviation and typical deviation from the curves): without β and without long trails −1.6 and 4.0 dB; with long trails +1.1 and 4.6 dB; with the angle β −5.4 and 6.2 dB, but with the best shape (3.0 dB once the mean deviation is removed, versus 3.6): the deep minima with a low radiant appear (Barcelona −15.6 dB at 17, versus −16 dB at 19:36; Sofia −18.5 dB at 20, versus −14 dB). With β and long trails ("As DJ5HG" preset) −2.2 and 4.7 dB; the cautious preset (radar height, 89.5 km, with β, without long trails) gives −6.9 and 7.6 dB, with shape 3.3 dB. Without β the program barely sees the minimum with the low radiant almost aligned with the path (−8.6 and −10.4 dB): this is the case of DJ5HG's reservation, which is why the warning remains.
La documentazione di MS-Soft 5.2 [29] de: The MS-Soft 5.2 documentation [29] defines OH5IY's efficiency as a relative index for underdense trails only, with two factors: radiant elevation (optimum about 45°) and angle with the path (90° = maximum). The minimum is raised by hand to 20 % for overdense trails; the formula is not published. MCG_MS [3] calculates the efficiency for four fixed directions and, when the DX station's locator is entered, also for the real path.

5.6 Zone PREV in pianta e sezione vista: 5.6 PREV zones in plan view and section seen from the antenna
Per l'ora mostrata il programma somma, p: For the time shown the program sums, point by point of the E layer, the contribution of each active shower to the efficiency (the same specular reflection condition as in chapter 5), weighted by the ZHR. The points with at least 3 % of the maximum form the PREV zones, one per side of the path, drawn in plan view as ellipses: centre = weighted mean of the points, axes = twice their spread. This is the practical rule: if the shower moves from north to south, the useful trails fall to the east and west. The yellow line shows the direction of motion (radiant azimuth) of the selected shower, or of the most favourable one.
La sezione mostra le stesse scie viste d: The section shows the same trails seen from the station with the antenna pointed towards the DX station: horizontally the azimuth relative to the DX station (A on the left, B on the right), vertically the elevation. For each shower the 14 strongest reflection points are taken; each trail is a segment oriented towards the radiant, from 10 km above to 10 km below the trail height (at most 60 km per side), thicker the more probable it is. Also drawn are the antenna lobe (−3 dB circle around the lobe elevation), the DX station and Hot A / Hot B.
Equazione di McKinley [8] e della Raccom: Equation of McKinley [8] and of Recommendation ITU-R P.843 [28] for underdense trails (sin α = 1), antenna gains excluded; q electron line density of the trail, re classical electron radius = 2.818·10⁻¹⁵ m, β angle between the trail and the plane of the path, a1 initial-radius factor of the trail r0 (P.843, eq. 4 and 7; r0 in m, h height in km):
Nel bilancio si usa β = 90° (scia che at: The budget uses β = 90° (trail crossing the plane of the path, the least favourable case: a cautious value) and also shows the best case, β = 0. The initial radius is calculated at the trail height used by the program; it is not added to the rules between bands (λ³ of SM6FHZ), because those rules are experimental and already contain it.
Con q = 10¹⁴ elettroni/m, scie a 89,5 km: With q = 10¹⁴ electrons/m, trails at 89.5 km and β = 0, at 144 MHz the result is 182–192 dB between 600 and 2100 km (185 dB at 1000 km). The range of 172–190 dB calculated by John Worsnop G4BAO in his doctoral thesis, quoted by GM8JBJ [9], includes these values. With β = 90° the loss increases by 10 dB at 600 km, 13 dB at 1000 km and 16 dB at 2100 km: OH5IY's average of 200 dB cited in the article [1] lies between the two cases. Again according to GM8JBJ, G4BAO finds about 6 dB less for trails aligned with the path.
I 182 dB della tabella di GM8JBJ [9] non: The 182 dB of GM8JBJ's table [9] are not a confirmation: the table does not state the frequency, its 86.4 dB per leg are the free-space loss over 500 km at 1 MHz (the 20 log f term is missing: at 144 MHz it is 129.6 dB) and the sum of the entries, 86.4 + 0 − 9 + 86.4, is 163.8 dB and not 182. The page mentions neither a minimum value nor 144 MHz.
Raggio iniziale alla quota media degli e: Initial radius at the mean echo height, h = 124 − 17 log f [28]: r0 = 0.76 m at 95 km for 50 MHz, 0.40 m at 87 km for 144 MHz, 0.21 m at 79 km for 432 MHz. Over 1000 km a1 is 0.2 dB at 50 MHz, 0.6 dB at 144 MHz and 1.4 dB at 432 MHz (2.9 dB at 600 km). At DJ5HG's fixed height of 102 km it would give about 70 dB at 432 MHz, i.e. no echo: this is why the mean echo height at the frequency is used.
I guadagni d'antenna si usano in dBi, se: Antenna gains are used in dBi, without subtracting the 2.15 dB of the dipole: McKinley's loss refers to isotropic antennas. Thus EIRP = power + gain, as in the article [1] (400 W and 14 dBi give about +70 dBm).
Guadagno di una Yagi lunga in funzione d: Gain of a long Yagi as a function of the boom length L (DL6WU curve [10], valid from about 2 λ):
Verifica con le simulazioni NEC di W4RNL: Check against W4RNL's NEC simulations at 432 MHz [12][19][20]: DL6WU 13, 22 and 31 elements (3.23 / 6.82 / 10.42 λ) 15.28 / 17.82 / 19.35 dBi, formula 15.38 / 17.91 / 19.34 dBi; David Tanner's VK3AUU Yagi, with a shorter boom for the same number of elements, 16, 28 and 40 elements (3.12 / 6.88 / 10.79 λ) 15.17 / 17.91 / 19.46 dBi, formula 15.27 / 17.94 / 19.45 dBi. The deviation does not exceed 0.1 dB: the gain depends on the boom length more than on the design. VK5DJ's calculator [21] also offers estimates for the VK3AUU, WA2PHW and DJ9BV variants, whose formulas are not published.
Apertura a −3 dB dal guadagno, regola di: −3 dB beamwidth from the gain, Kraus's rule [11], with a circular lobe (θE = θH = θK):
Le simulazioni NEC delle Yagi DL6WU [19]: NEC simulations of DL6WU Yagis [19] give a horizontal lobe 5–10 % narrower than Kraus: 33.8° / 26.4° / 22.6° for 12, 19 and 26 elements, versus Kraus's 37.3° / 28.0° / 23.9°. The simple formulas ignore the forward sidelobes [12]. On long booms the vertical lobe is slightly wider than the horizontal one (14 λ: 18.4° / 18.8°).
Lobo orizzontale (piano E, azimut con po: Horizontal lobe (E plane, azimuth with horizontal polarisation) = 0.93 · θK; vertical lobe (H plane) = θK. Approximate rules, derived from a few DL6WU antennas:
Yagi di 14 λ a 432 MHz: 20,3 dBi, lobo 1: 14 λ Yagi at 432 MHz: 20.3 dBi, lobe 18.1° horizontal and 19.5° vertical. W4RNL's models [12] give 20.4 dBi and 18.4° / 18.8°.
L'antenna si considera puntata verso il: The antenna is considered pointed towards the DX station. A hot spot (section 4.5) is within the lobe if |Az(Hot) − Az(antenna)| ≤ θhor/2: in that case it is marked in grey instead of pink and the main window shows a warning. The hot spot recommended by the efficiency (section 4.6) is always in red.
Il grafico SKiYMET di Collm [7] (720×720: The SKiYMET plot of Collm [7] (720×720 pixels, pure colours) has fixed axis positions, but every day the radar adapts the vertical scale to the measured values (for example 0–1.2 ·10³ on 5/11/2026 and 0–1.0 ·10³ on 6/11/2026, with shifted tick marks). The program finds the long tick marks of the axis and reads the labels of the highest and the lowest (0.0) by comparing each character with the templates of the plot's dot-matrix font. For the i-th hour (0–47, yesterday and today) the central column and the first cyan pixel from the top y give:
ytop e y0 sono le righe della tacca più: ytop and y0 are the rows of the highest tick mark and of the zero tick mark, Ntop the value read on the highest label (×1000). The resolution is about 7–8 meteors/hour per pixel. Regole sperimentali di SM6FHZ [4]: il nu: Experimental rules of SM6FHZ [4]: the number (and intensity) of reflections scales with λ³, the duration with λ². With f0 = 36.2 MHz (Collm) and f the target frequency:
La durata di una scia sottodensa vale τ: The duration of an underdense trail is τ = λ²·sec²φ / (16π²D), with D the diffusion coefficient (McKinley [8]; OH5IY [29]; IZ5TEK [30]). The Collm radar measures in backscatter (φ = 0); on a forward-scatter path the duration increases by sec²φ, with φ at the midpoint: ×4 at 60°, ×8.5 at 70°, ×33 at 80°. The Experimental forecasts sub-tab applies it.
In McKinley [8] λ³ è la potenza di una s: In McKinley [8] λ³ is the power of a single underdense trail, not the number of trails. At a fixed threshold and with mass index s, the number of trails above the threshold scales with λ raised to 1.5·(s − 1), i.e. about λ^1.5 for s = 2 (IZ5TEK [30]; OH5IY [29]). The program keeps k = 3, the experimental rule of SM6FHZ [4], and says so: with k = 3, 1000 meteors/hour at Collm become about 16 reflections/hour at 144 MHz, with k = 1.5 about 127. RMOB observers of the GRAVES radar at 143.050 MHz [13] typically count 20 to 140 echoes/hour; the right value of k for one's own station is obtained from the comparison with RMOB (next section).

Misure reali (HamSCI, Meteor Scatter QSO: Real measurements (HamSCI, Meteor Scatter QSO Party [33]): R. Suggs NN4NT measured the power decay constant of 1298 underdense echoes in the MSK144 recordings of NN4SA (EM64) during the 2026 Perseids (4736 WSJT-X WAV files). Medians: 148 ms at 28.145 MHz (41 echoes), 78 ms at 50.260 MHz (1198), 53 ms at 144.150 MHz (59). With λ² starting from 6 m they would be about 245 ms and 9.5 ms: on 2 m pings last more than five times longer than predicted. The author attributes this to a probable echo ceiling height effect on 2 m: at high frequencies mainly the low trails remain visible, where diffusion is slower. It is a preliminary analysis: a single receiving station, different distances not normalised with sec²φ, only echoes strong enough to be detected.
Weitzen e Ralston [31]: la costante di d: Weitzen and Ralston [31]: the decay constant varies from trail to trail with an exponential distribution, with mean τ = λ²·sec²φ / (32π²D) (power constant; 16π² applies to the amplitude). Xia, Li and Zheng [32] give D as a function of height, D = 10^(0.067·h − 5.6) m²/s: over 1000 km with the trail at 95 km this gives τ ≈ 47 ms at 144 MHz and 390 ms at 50 MHz. The 144 MHz value is close to the measured median, the 50 MHz one is five times higher: D grows tenfold every 15 km of height, so the height of the visible trails, which changes with frequency, weighs on the duration more than λ².
Il programma offre la scelta \"Durata de: The program offers the choice "Ping duration between bands" in the Geometry and path loss sub-tab. Theoretical (default, cautious): λ², which gives the shortest pings. Observed: linear interpolation on a logarithmic scale between the three NN4SA medians; below 28 MHz the 10–6 m segment is extended, above 144 MHz, where there are no measurements, λ² is used again. With the observed choice a 1 s echo at Collm (36.2 MHz) lasts about 473 ms at 144 MHz instead of 63 ms, and from 50 to 144 MHz pings become 1.5 times shorter instead of 8.
Incertezza del raggio iniziale: Stober e: Uncertainty of the initial radius: Stober et al. [34], with the CMOR radar at 17.45, 29.85 and 38.15 MHz and a full wave scattering model, find between 85 and 95 km r0 of 0.5–2 m, mostly 1–1.5 m, with a scatter of a factor of two at each height; for transverse polarisation the values are about twice the earlier measurements (Greenhow and Hall 1960; Jones and Campbell-Brown 2005). Only about 5 % of echoes can be described by the ideal model. The ITU-R P.843 formula [28] gives 0.5 m at 90 km and 0.75 m at 95 km, i.e. the lower limit of these measurements.
Il programma offre la scelta \"Raggio in: The program offers the choice "Initial trail radius" in the Geometry and path loss sub-tab: twice the ITU value (default, cautious, like the measurements of Stober et al.), ITU-R P.843, excluded. Doubling r0 multiplies the factor a1 in dB by 4: over 1000 km 0.8 dB at 50 MHz, 2.4 dB at 144 MHz and 5.6 dB at 432 MHz (11.6 dB at 600 km). The CMOR measurements are at lower frequencies and at 85–95 km: using them at 432 MHz, where echoes come from about 79 km, is an extrapolation.
Due tesi sulla direzione migliore del ra: Two views on the best radiant direction. The classic radio amateur view: the best radiant is between 15° and 70° high and broadside to the path, one aligned with the path is marginal. It is held by SM6FHZ [4] with his experimental rules, by DH9GCD with his formula (reported by DF5HC [17]) and by meteor-mcp from qso-graph [35], which grounds it on the tangency condition: useful trails must be tangent to an ellipsoid with its foci at the two stations, and those running along the path rarely are. This view counts where trails can reflect, but not how much each one reflects.
Tesi della formula completa: McKinley [8: The full-formula view: McKinley [8] and ITU-R P.843 [28] give the power of each trail the factor 1 / (1 − cos²β sin²φ), where β is the angle between the trail and the path plane. A trail lying in the plane (β = 0) reflects 1/cos²φ times more than one crossing it (β = 90°): 10-15 dB between 600 and 2000 km. With the radiant aligned with the path the tangent trails lie close to the plane and weigh more; with the radiant broadside they cross it and weigh less. DJ5HG [22] uses the same factor, and his hourly curves have the shape that YA-MS finds with β on (shape deviation about 3 dB).
Le due tesi usano la stessa condizione d: The two views use the same specular reflection condition but weight the trails differently: the classic one counts the useful trails, the full one also weighs their power. Over 1000 km, with the radiant at 30°, the perpendicular radiant is worth 67 % without β and 15 % with β. Neither has yet been compared with independent counts per shower and per path: that comparison can decide, for example with receiver networks such as BRAMS.
Nel programma la casella \"Angolo β tra: In the program the box "Angle β between trail and path (full McKinley)" is on by default because it overestimates no trail (cautious value); off, it applies the classic view. The box "Classic verdict" adds under each shower, in the hourly table, the row of the classic verdict computed at the path midpoint: ✗ radiant below the horizon, ◐ marginal (below 15° or above 70°, or less than 30° from the path direction), ● good, ★ best (between 15° and 70° and more than 60° from the path direction), with the thresholds of meteor-mcp [35]. It does not change the calculation: it shows hour by hour where the two views agree and where they do not.
Confronto con il catalogo dell'IAU Meteo: Comparison with the catalogue of the IAU Meteor Data Center [36]: the Showers tab shows for each shower how many solutions are published in the list of established showers and the difference between the program's IMO catalogue and the median of the solutions: angular distance of the radiants (compared at the same solar longitude, with the program's drift), Δλ (the program's λ max minus the median of the mean solar longitudes of activity, which do not exactly coincide with the maximum) and Δv. The tooltip lists the solutions with their references. The original file is downloaded at most once a month from www.ta3.sk; the MDC asks to cite Jenniskens et al. 2020 and Jopek and Kaňuchová 2017.
Il pulsante \"k dagli indici di popolazi: The "k from population indices" button computes for each active shower k = 1.5·(s − 1) with s = 1 + 2.5·log10 r, i.e. k = 3.75·log10 r, and takes the ZHR-weighted mean. The population index r comes from the table on the Global Meteor Network flux page [37] when available, otherwise from the IMO catalogue [5]; the Showers tab shows k for each shower. Examples: Perseids r = 2.2, k = 1.28; Geminids r = 2.6, k = 1.56. The default stays k = 3 from SM6FHZ [4], more cautious; the Collm counts, however, are mostly sporadic meteors, for which GMN does not publish r.
Conteggi del Global Meteor Network [37]:: Global Meteor Network counts [37]: in the Live showers tab and in the "GMN today" column of the Showers tab the program reads the daily summary of trajectories confirmed by the network's cameras (one line per meteor, with the IAU shower code or "..." for sporadics) and counts them by shower. It is a count, not a flux: it depends on how many stations have a clear, dark sky. Data CC BY 4.0.
Le due tesi usano la stessa condizione d: The two views use the same specular reflection condition but weight the trails differently: the classic one counts the useful trails, the full one also weighs their power. Over 1000 km, with the radiant at 30°, the perpendicular radiant is worth 67 % without β and 15 % with β. A first comparison with real counts does not tell them apart (next paragraph): deciding needs longer paths and more receivers.
Confronto con conteggi reali: rilevament: Comparison with real counts: BRAMS detections received at Sonneberg (Dourbes beacon, 49.97 MHz, 471 km path) from 12 to 28 August 2026, about 97 000 echoes detected with the method of M. Bundscherer [38]. After removing the background (hour-by-hour median from 22 to 27 August), the Perseids add at most, on 13 August between 02 and 10 UTC, about 80-130 echoes/hour on top of 300-470: at 50 MHz they weigh little compared with the sporadics. The hourly excess follows the YA-MS calculation (Perseid efficiency × ZHR) with a correlation of 0.44 with β on and 0.43 with β off, the same as ZHR times the sine of the radiant elevation; with long trails it drops to 0.36. On this short path the geometry adds no information and the comparison does not decide between the two views. Limits: a single receiver, an adaptive detection threshold that can reduce the counts in the busiest hours, minor showers still active on the background days, beacon antenna pointing at the zenith.
Il programma divide lo strato E in punti: The program divides the E layer into points every 15 km and keeps those that both stations see above the horizon. With the "antenna pattern" box on (default) each point is weighted with the vertical gain of the two antennas: a beam fixed at 0° still has its main lobe a few degrees above the horizon because of the ground reflection, and the "Lobe elevation" is the elevation e0 of that peak. With e the elevation of the point seen from a station and θV the vertical width of the lobe at −3 dB (chapter 7):
g(e) = 10^(−1,2·(e/θV)²) · sin²(π/2 · si: g(e) = 10^(−1.2·(e/θV)²) · sin²(π/2 · sin e / sin e0) for e < e0;   g(e) = 10^(−1.2·(e/θV)²) for e ≥ e0;   point weight × g(e1) · g(e2)
Sotto il massimo il fattore del terreno: Below the peak the ground factor brings the gain to zero at the horizon; the lobe has a floor of −20 dB. A low point counts less, but it counts: on a long path the efficiency does not vanish. With the box off the lobe elevation is a hard limit, as up to version 1.8.0: points seen below e0 by either station do not count, and on a long path with the lobe a few degrees up all efficiencies can be 0 (JN70CN – JO76QP, 1791 km, lobe at 3°, trails at 88.5 km: no point).
Il lobo verticale è un modello semplice:: The vertical lobe is a simple model: horizontal antenna, Gaussian lobe θV wide at −3 dB (Kraus) and ground factor up to the first peak; the further lobes, the real antenna height and the surrounding terrain are not considered.

Confronto con gli spot reali: 181 767 sp: Comparison with real spots: 181,767 MSK144 spots on 50 MHz from the HamSCI Meteor Scatter QSO Party of 11-12 August 2025 (Perseids, stations almost all North American, 5207 paths between 300 and 2300 km) [39]. Hour by hour, the number of paths with spots follows the path index computed by the program: correlation 0.77 with the β angle on and 0.66 with β off (on ranks 0.72 and 0.68), with the maximum between 10 and 12 UTC on both days; those hours, however, also coincide with the maximum of sporadic meteors and with operator activity. With the same stations active in the same hour, neither the program (β on or off) nor the DH9GCD formula distinguishes the pairs that heard each other from those that did not (AUC 0.51-0.53, where 0.5 is chance): which pair hears each other depends on sporadic meteors, which the index does not contain, and on activity. These data confirm the hourly trend but do not distinguish between the two theses on β. Tools: the program's --indici-tratte option and tools/verifica_spot.py.
